ai.definition: Omni-Present Ambient Intelligence is an IoT technology that leverages edge AI to predict human needs by fusing data from multiple sensors such as those tracking gait, voice, and biometrics.
ai.howItWorks: The system uses a mesh network of sensors to collect telemetry data. This data is processed locally using edge AI algorithms to infer user needs without requiring explicit prompts. The predictions are then used to automate responses or trigger actions in the environment.
ai.problemSolved: Reduces the need for direct user interaction and enhances efficiency by anticipating user needs, thereby improving overall convenience and productivity in environments like smart cities and homes.
ai.manufacturing: Involves designing and fabricating sensor nodes, developing edge AI algorithms, and setting up a mesh network infrastructure. The manufacturing process requires precision in component assembly and robustness to ensure reliable data transmission over long periods.
ai.buildProcess: Sensor nodes are designed with low-power microcontrollers and integrated sensors for gait, voice, and biometric tracking. Edge AI algorithms are trained on large datasets to recognize patterns and predict user needs. The mesh network is configured to enable seamless data exchange between nodes.
ai.costDrivers: High initial investment in sensor node design, edge AI development, and network infrastructure setup. Ongoing costs include maintenance of the network and updates to AI models as new data becomes available.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to transition from lab research to early commercial deployment within a few years due to increasing demand for smart environments and advancements in sensor technology.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks will need to address privacy concerns related to continuous monitoring and data collection. Standards for interoperability between different sensor types and network protocols may also be required.
ai.risks: Privacy issues, potential security vulnerabilities, and the risk of false predictions leading to inappropriate actions are significant challenges that must be mitigated through robust design and stringent testing.
ai.profitability: Potential for high profitability in the smart home and city sectors if successful deployment can lead to increased user adoption and reduced operational costs over time.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future advancements may include more sophisticated AI models, integration with other IoT technologies, and enhanced security features. The technology could also evolve to support a wider range of applications beyond homes and cities.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking processes required for certain sensor components.

glossary.def: Artificial intelligence processing that occurs at or near the source of data, reducing latency and bandwidth requirements.
A decentralized wireless network where each node can communicate with its neighboring nodes, allowing for robust and flexible communication paths.

subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: gathers raw signals about people and the space without asking anyone to press a button.
parts: temperature, humidity, light and door sensors

subsystems.name: Connectivity mesh
subsystems.role: moves that data between devices with low latency and local fallback when the internet is down.
parts: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Low Energy links

subsystems.name: Edge inference compute
subsystems.role: runs recognition models next to the sensors so raw data need not leave the building.

subsystems.name: Context fusion engine
subsystems.role: turns separate streams into one model of who is present, where, and what they are doing.
parts: a live digital model of the space

subsystems.name: Personalisation and policy layer
subsystems.role: learns routines and enforces the rules about what may be sensed, stored or shared.

subsystems.name: Actuation and feedback
subsystems.role: changes the environment and quietly tells people what it has done.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the space
buildSteps.detail: Fit radar and microphone modules in ceilings and walls, add door, window and environmental sensors, and reuse existing Wi-Fi access points as sensing radios.

buildSteps.title: Commission the mesh
buildSteps.detail: Join every device to a local network with a border router, assign stable addresses and confirm each one still works if the internet link drops.

buildSteps.title: Collect consented data
buildSteps.detail: With explicit agreement, record labelled examples of daily activities, plus synthetic and simulated data to cover rare events.

buildSteps.title: Train and compress models
buildSteps.detail: Train activity, occupancy and gait models on the labelled set, then quantise and prune them until they fit the memory and power budget of the edge hardware.

buildSteps.title: Deploy inference locally
buildSteps.detail: Run the models on a home hub or on the devices themselves, and tune confidence thresholds so the system stays silent rather than acting wrongly.

buildSteps.title: Fuse streams into context
buildSteps.detail: Combine the separate detections into a single state — room, person, activity, confidence — and resolve conflicts between sensors.

buildSteps.title: Set the policy layer
buildSteps.detail: Define what is sensed, what is kept, how long it is kept and what may be shared, defaulting to local-only processing with a visible override.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop and retrain
buildSteps.detail: Let actuators respond, record whether each action was wanted, and periodically retrain without exporting raw personal data.

prerequisites.why: recognition has to run continuously on small devices within a few watts.
Wi-Fi channel-state and radar sensing can detect presence and movement through walls, but reliability varies between rooms and furniture layouts.
a common application layer lets devices from different makers share context instead of each running an isolated app.
personalisation must improve from many users without pooling their raw sensor data centrally.
a system that predicts needs cannot go blind when a battery or router fails.

pathway.milestone: single-purpose ambient products — voice assistants, occupancy-aware heating, automatic fall alerts
pathway.unlocks: proves individual sensing tasks work in ordinary homes.

pathway.milestone: room-level multimodal context running on a local hub using a common device standard
pathway.unlocks: fewer false triggers, so automation becomes trustworthy enough to leave switched on.

pathway.milestone: federated personalisation across homes and buildings
pathway.unlocks: routines learned from many users while raw data stays on site.

pathway.milestone: building- and district-scale coordination of energy, lighting and access
pathway.unlocks: demand that follows people, cutting wasted energy in cities.
